newsitem.title: ANGOLA: DeBeers sees Angola project as stabilizing.
newsitem.headline: DeBeers sees Angola project as stabilizing.

text.p: A diamond-sorting center that De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd plans to build in the Angolan capital should help to restore order to that country's diamond market, a senior De Beers official said Thursday.

"One of the problems we have been faced with in Angola is that there are no facilities," De Beers' Oliver Oliveira, director of the Central Selling Office in London, told Reuters during a visit to the Angolan capital city of Luanda.
"We hope that with this new plant we can help bring some order to the diamond industry in Angola," he said.
De Beers said on Tuesday it had signed an agreement with Angola's state diamond company Endiama to build a 12-storey building to house a diamond-sorting center for Angolan diamonds.
It will build the $30 million facility in central Luanda on land leased from Endiama, which will own three floors of the building.
Oliveira also said the current system of valuing diamonds in Angola was difficult to control, and the company hoped to find a way to introduce an alternative method.

"We need to bring a consistent system of valuation to this system," Oliveira said. "The current system is extremely hard to control. Endiama now values the diamonds, and they do not value the same way we do."
Oliveira said the new state-of-the-art building would take up to three years to complete.
"The lighting has to be just right and the security, of course, is important," he said. "We will have to have some very sophisticated security controls."
Angola produces around $1 billion in diamonds each year.
De Beers, which has four established buying offices in Angola, also has agreements with Endiama to prospect for new kimberlites in three areas.
